intro.title: Zero Hunger
intro.Description: The second sustainable goal we have chosen is Zero Hunger, this goal focuses on ending hunger, achieving food security and improved nutrition and promoting sustainable agriculture

whyThisGoalMatters.Heading: Why this goal matters
whyThisGoalMatters.text: Zero hunger means less children than ever before will be born into food insecurity, giving them a fairer and healthier start in life. When everybody has access to nutritious, safe and sufficient food they are able to grow and develop to their full potential, leading to healthier and more productive lives. Achieving zero hunger also means that we are supporting sustainable agriculture, which is vital for protecting the environment and combating climate change.

localPolicies.Heading: Local Policies to support Zero Hunger

policies.Text: Target 2.1 states that by 2030 the aim is to end hunger and ensure access by all people, in particular the poor and people in vulnerable situations, including infants, to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round. As a policy maker you play a significant role in determining funding for food banks, a heavily relied on resource, by allocating more funding you can make sure less children go hungry in your local area.
Target 2.a focuses on increasing investment especially in rural infrastructure, agricultural research etc. as a policy maker you can ensure farmers are protected and supported.

Target 2.c focuses on adopting measures to ensure the proper functioning of food commodity markets and their derivatives and facilitate timely access to market information, including on food reserves, in order to help limit extreme food price volatility, as a policymaker you can ensure there is adequate food reserves so that everyone in your community can access affordable food.

additionalResources.Heading: Additional Resources
additionalResources.text: If you are interested in learning more about how you can contribute to achieving our 3 goals, there are many reliable resources that can offer guidance, information and practical actions that you can take. Understanding the causes of Gender inequality, Food insecurity and unsustainability can help you as a policy maker make more informed decisions. The united nations, Linked below, provides extensive information on all of these topics and more. Including explanations of the adversities people and communities face and continue to face bopth around the world and in our local area. In addition to our three names goals on this website the United Nations also tracks progress on all of its other Sustainable Development Goals, offering not only updated statistics but also current global efforts and detailed descriptions of each target. By exploring these resources you can better understand how all these goals connect to eachother and why they are so essential for creating a more sustainable, just and inclusive world.

intro1.title: Gender Equality
intro1.Description: The second sustainable goal we have chosen is to achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls.

whyThisGoalMatters1.Heading: Why this goal matters
whyThisGoalMatters1.text: Achieving this goal isnt only a moral imperative, it is also an incredibly powerful driver of progress. When women and girls have equal access to employment, education and oppurtunities, communities and economies thrive and grow. The closing of the gender gap benefits everyone. A safer, healthier and more inclusive world can be created through the abolishment of gender inequality.

localPolicies1.Heading: Possible policies to make change at the local level

policies.Text: Target 5.5 of the sustainable development goals is to Ensure women's full and effective participation in leadership and decision-making. As policy makers you should ensure inclusion of women and hire more women in prominent roles. You should also encourage companies and corporations to include more women in leadership roles. You can do this by helping promote fundraising towards women's rights and education organisations that help advance women despite the barriers they face.

Target 5.2 of the SDG is to end all violence against women and girls. As policy makers you have the power to protect women from violence and exploitation. You can create policies to enforce women's safety and prevent exploitation like policing dangerous areas and providing better avenues for reporting sexual crimes. This goal is especially important as in the past couple decades sexual violence against women and girls has risen significantly showing a lack of action to protect women and girls.

Target 5.3 of the sustainable development goals is to eliminate forced marriages and any other harmful practices such as female genital mutilation. While this isn't an issue local to your area it is still important that you take part in action to help get rid of these practices world wide as they are still prevalent issues in many parts of the world. As a policy maker you could help push for initiatives to raise awareness and help facilitate charity functions in your area. You could also push for legislation that criminalises taking women children abroad to countries where it is legal to force them to marry.

intro2.title: Sustainable Cities and Communities
intro2.Description: The first sustainable goal we have chosen is to create new sustainable cities/communities and to improve the sustainability of existing cities/communities.

whyThisGoalMatters2.Heading: Why this goal matters
whyThisGoalMatters2.text: Sustainable cities and Communities means future and current cities and human settlements will be more inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable than ever before. With more than half of the world's population living in urban areas, and this number expected to increase to nearly 70% by 2050, it is crucial that we focus on making our cities more sustainable. Sustainable cities can help reduce poverty and inequality, improve health and well-being, and promote economic growth. They can also help mitigate the impacts of climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainable transportation and energy use.

localPolicies2.Heading: Local Policies to support Sustainable Cities and Communities

policies.Text: Target 11.1 of the sustainable cities and communities goal states that by 2030 we should have ensured that all have access to adequate, safe and affordable housing and basic services. As policy makers you have the power to push through legislation in your local area that combats homelessness and inadequate housing.

Target 11.4 of the Sustainable Cities and Communities goal focuses on strengthening efforts to protect and safeguard the entire world’s cultural and natural heritage. Included in this is everything from historic buildings and sacred sites to traditional practices, languages, and landscapes that hold significance for communities. Ensuring these elements are preserved is essential because they not only connect us to our past they also shape our identity and provide invaluable knowledge for future generations.As a policy maker, you have the power to ensure that nobody's culture or heritage is threatened or forgotten. You can support this by encouraging schools to teach students about the importance of cultural and natural heritage, helping young people understand why these sites and traditions matter and why it is therefore essential to preserve and protect them. You can also organise or promote fundraising events to provide financial resources for conserving and restoring world heritage sites. By taking these actions, you help protect the stories, environments, and traditions that make our world rich, diverse, and meaningful.

Target 11.6 of the sustainable cities and communities goal is to by 2030, reduce the adverse per capita environmental impact of cities, including by paying specicial attention to air quality and municipal and other waste management, as a policy maker you can encourage legislation and education on recycling and its importance to ensure responsible waste management.
